# Project file

<!-- Generated by `chipload reference`; do not edit. Regenerate with CHIPLOAD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p chipload-cli --test guide. -->

A project (`.chipload`) is a JSON file. Chipload writes every field; when you write one by hand or with a script, the fields marked *no* may be left out. Lengths are in mm, angles in radians, feeds in mm/min. `chipload schema project` prints the JSON Schema this page is made from.

Schema version 40. Older files load through Chipload's migrations; this schema describes only the current version.

## The file

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active_part` | integer or null | no | The part new operations go into (its id). Null or no such part: the first part. Only the app and the command line read it; it changes nothing that is cut. |
| `active_setup` | integer or null | no | The setup shown, simulated and previewed, where new parts go (its id). Null or no such setup: the first. Only the app and the command line read it. |
| `drawing` | [Drawing](#drawing) | yes | The drawing: the shapes Chipload cuts, imported from a DXF or drawn in Chipload. |
| `machine` | [Machine](#machine) | yes | The machine: post-processor, safe height, limits. |
| `operations` | list of [Operation](#operation) | yes | The operations, cut in this order: grouped by part, in the parts' order. |
| `parts` | list of [Part](#part) | yes | The parts: groups of operations, each cut with its copies before the next part. At least one. |
| `schema_version` | `40` | yes | The version of the file format. Chipload upgrades older files when it reads them, and refuses newer ones. |
| `setups` | list of [Setup](#setup) | yes | The setups: each a board clamped on the machine, with its stock, its work zero and the parts cut from it, written as a program of its own. At least one. Since schema 34. |
| `tools` | list of [Tool](#tool) | yes | The tools the operations cut with. |
| `written_by` | string or null | no | The Chipload version that wrote the file, for reference. |

## ArcSegment

From `start_angle` through `sweep` radians (positive = counter-clockwise).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | 2 × number | yes | Centre, mm. |
| `radius` | number | yes | Radius, mm. |
| `start_angle` | number | yes | Where the arc starts, radians from +X, counter-clockwise. |
| `sweep` | number | yes | How far it turns, radians: positive counter-clockwise. |

## AutoThreshold

The word "auto".

One of: `"auto"`.

## Axis

An axis of the drawing.

One of: `"x"`, `"y"`.

## BackOf

Which setup a back setup turns over, and how (docs/specs/two-sided.md §3).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register` | [Register](#register) | yes | How the turned board is put back in place. |
| `setup` | integer | yes | The id of the front setup: the board as it lies first. |
| `turn` | [Turn](#turn) | yes | How the board is turned over. |

## Bone

What a chosen corner gets.

One of: `"none"`, `"dogbone"`, `"tbone"`.

## ClearingPass

A clearing pass with its own end mill, inside an operation's shapes and depths: a pocket's rest pass (docs/specs/rest-passes.md §2: an endmill smaller than the tool before it, clearing only what that tool leaves) or a V-carve's floor pass (docs/specs/vcarve-wide-strokes.md §4: an end mill clearing the floor between the walls, before the V-carve).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: kept, but not cut. Missing: true. |
| `entry` | [Entry](#entry) | yes | How the tool goes down: `plunge`, `ramp` or `helix`. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `slot_feed` | number or null | no | As a pocket's `slot_feed`. Null: `feed`. |
| `slot_step_down` | number or null | no | As a pocket's `slot_step_down`. Null: `step_down`. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between the clearing rings, as a fraction of the tool diameter. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`): an end mill. |

## CornerChoice

A corner with its own bone, chosen by the user.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `along` | [Wall](#wall) or null | no | The wall a T-bone runs along, `longer` or `shorter`: the notch is in the other. Required with a T-bone; null otherwise. |
| `at` | 2 × number | yes | The corner, in drawing coordinates (mm). |
| `bone` | [Bone](#bone) | yes | `none` (the corner stays round), `dogbone` or `tbone`. |

## Corners

How the tool reaches into the inside corners it would leave round, so a square part fits: every corner on the tool's side up to `max_angle`.

### `"type": "dogbone"`

In along the corner's bisector.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_angle` | number | yes | Only corners this sharp or sharper, radians (1.745 = 100°). |

### `"type": "tbone"`

In along the longer wall: the notch is in the shorter one.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_angle` | number | yes | Only corners this sharp or sharper, radians (1.745 = 100°). |

## CustomPost

A user post-processor's config and template, exactly as read from the posts folder.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config` | string | yes | The post's settings file (TOML), as copied. |
| `template` | string | yes | The post's template, as copied. |

## Direction

One of: `"climb"`, `"conventional"`.

## Drawing

The project's drawing: shapes in millimetres, or (only for jobs from before v4) a reference to a DXF that still has to be embedded.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dxfs` | list of [DrawingSource](#drawingsource) | no | The DXFs the imported shapes came from, each as at its last import or update, with its own placement. |
| `frames` | list of [Frame](#frame) | no | Frames for signs that are drawn again round what they go round when it changes. Left out of the file when there are none, so projects without them open in older versions. |
| `groups` | list of [ShapeGroup](#shapegroup) | no | Groups of drawn shapes and texts, selected, moved and cut as one. Left out of the file when there are none, so projects without groups open in older versions. |
| `hidden` | list of string | no | Groups and layers not drawn on the canvas (they are still cut): `dxf:1`, `dxf:1/layer:Cut`, `image:1`, `text:1`, `drawn:circle`, `drawn:rectangle`, `drawn:polyline`. |
| `images` | list of [Image](#image) | no | Pictures traced into shapes, for V-carving. |
| `models` | list of [Model](#model) | no | 3D models carved as reliefs from the top. Left out of the file when there are none, so projects without them open in older versions, which refuse one with them. |
| `next_shape_id` | integer | yes | The id the next new shape gets. Ids are never reused. |
| `shapes` | list of [Shape](#shape) | yes | The shapes, imported and drawn. |
| `texts` | list of [Text](#text) | no | Texts written into shapes, for V-carving, pocketing or profiling. Left out of the file when there are none, so projects without text open in older versions. |

## DrawingFormat

A drawing file's format.

One of: `"dxf"`, `"svg"`.

## DrawingSource

Provenance of the imported shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | yes | The DXF's file name. |
| `flattened` | object | no | How many curves of each type (splines, ellipses) were turned into arcs. |
| `format` | [DrawingFormat](#drawingformat) | yes | What kind of file it is: a DXF or an SVG. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The DXF's id, which its shapes and selectors name. |
| `ignored` | object | no | How many entities of each type were left out (text, dimensions, …). |
| `imported` | object | no | How many entities of each type were imported. |
| `issues` | list of [SourceIssue](#sourceissue) | no | What the import found: the import report. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name in the Browser and messages; the file's name without its extension at first. |
| `placement` | [Placement](#placement) | yes | How the imported drawing was moved, turned and scaled on the stock. |
| `px_per_inch` | number or null | no | An SVG without a real size: the pixels per inch chosen for it, used again on update. None for a DXF and an SVG with real units. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The DXF's SHA-256, to tell whether it changed. |
| `units` | [Units](#units) | yes | The DXF's units: `mm` or `inch`. Inch drawings are converted to mm on import. |
| `units_from` | [UnitsFrom](#unitsfrom) | yes | Where the units came from: the DXF itself, or the user's choice. |

## EdgeSide

Where a chamfer's waste is: around the shape (a part's outline) or within it (a hole's or a pocket's rim).

One of: `"outside"`, `"inside"`.

## Entry

How the tool goes down into the material at the start of each pass, for pockets and follow paths (a profile always spirals: its `ramp_angle`).

### `"type": "plunge"`

Straight down: needs a centre-cutting tool. An empty struct variant, as `Rings`.

### `"type": "ramp"`

Down along the path and back, never steeper than `ramp_angle` (radians, 0 < angle <= 30°).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the ramp goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |

### `"type": "helix"`

Pockets only: down round a circle of `radius` (the tool centre's), never steeper than `ramp_angle`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | yes | The helix's radius, mm: less than the tool radius. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the helix goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |

## FillPattern

The pattern a `PatternOp` engraves (docs/specs/fill-pattern.md §3). Angles in radians from the X axis, counter-clockwise; lengths in mm.

- object: Parallel straight lines, `spacing` apart (centre to centre), at `angle`.

- object: Two sets of lines: at `angle`, and at `angle` + `between` (more than 0, at most 90°).

- object: The shape's outline repeated inwards, `spacing` apart, as closed rings.

- object: Parallel sine waves at `angle`, `spacing` apart: `wavelength` long, `height` from top to bottom.

- object: Rows `spacing` apart of strokes `length` long with `gap` between, every other row shifted half a stroke and gap (docs/specs/fill-pattern.md §14).

- object: Columns of strokes `length` long at 45° to `angle`, `spacing` apart along the column, every other column mirrored, meeting in chevrons.

- object: Rows `spacing` apart of half circles of `radius` side by side, every other row shifted by a radius.

- object: Round the middle of each shape: rings `spacing` apart of strokes `length` long pointing outwards, `pitch` apart round the ring, every other ring turned half a pitch.

## Finish

A finishing pass on a profile.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stock` | number | yes | Left on the wall by the roughing passes, mm: more than 0, less than the tool radius. |

## Frame

A frame for a sign that follows what it goes round (docs/specs/sign-maker.md §4): its outline and border lines are ordinary drawn shapes, drawn again from these values when the texts or shapes it goes round change. Editing its shapes by hand ends that: the record goes and they stay as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `around` | [FrameAround](#framearound) or null | no | What it goes round. None: drawn to a size, following nothing. |
| `border_corners` | [FrameCorners](#framecorners) or null | no | The borders' own corner style, for a rectangular frame; None: they follow the outline's shape, each `gap` further in (docs/specs/sign-maker.md §5). |
| `border_width` | number | no | The width of a border's groove at the surface, mm: the margin is measured to its inner edge, and a double border's lines are twice it apart. 0: lines as drawn. |
| `borders` | list of integer | no | Its border lines inside the outline, outside in, by shape id. |
| `center` | 2 × number | yes | Where it was last drawn: the outline's centre, mm. |
| `corner` | number | yes | The corner size, mm: what it is depends on the kind (`chipload frame kinds`). |
| `double` | boolean | no | Each border two lines, twice `border_width` apart, which leaves a ridge as wide as a groove between them. |
| `gap` | number | yes | From the outline to the first border, and from one border to the next (from its inner line, for double borders), mm. |
| `height` | number | yes | The outline's height as last drawn, mm. |
| `kind` | [FrameShape](#frameshape) | yes | The outline's shape. |
| `margin` | number | yes | From the box of what it goes round to its innermost line, mm. |
| `outline` | integer | yes | Its outline, by shape id; the frame is named by it. |
| `width` | number | yes | The outline's width as last drawn, mm. |

## FrameAround

What a frame goes round: texts with all their letters, pictures with all their traced shapes, and other shapes, by id.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `images` | list of integer | no |  |
| `shapes` | list of integer | no |  |
| `texts` | list of integer | no |  |

## FrameCorners

The corner style of a rectangular frame's borders (docs/specs/sign-maker.md §5).

One of: `"sharp"`, `"round"`, `"notch"`, `"chamfer"`, `"step"`.

## FrameShape

A frame's outline (docs/specs/shape-library.md §3.1).

One of: `"rectangle"`, `"rounded"`, `"notched"`, `"chamfered"`, `"oval"`, `"arched"`, `"plaque"`, `"stepped"`, `"gable"`, `"double_arch"`, `"shield"`, `"banner"`, `"octagon"`.

## HoleMethod

How a Holes operation cuts.

### `"type": "drill"`

Straight down at the hole's centre, `peck` mm at a time.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `peck` | number or null | no | Drill this many mm at a time, lifting out between pecks to clear chips. Null: in one go. |

### `"type": "bore"`

A helix at the wall, at most `step_down` mm per turn and never steeper than `ramp_angle` (radians, 0 < angle <= 30°), then one level circle.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional`, as for a profile inside the hole. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the helix goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The most the helix goes down per turn, mm. |

## Image

A picture traced into shapes: the picture itself, where it goes, and how it becomes black and white. Its traced shapes are `path` shapes on its layer that name it in `image`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `arcs` | boolean | yes | Traced edges are fitted with arcs as well as lines. |
| `blur` | number | yes | Blur before the threshold, in pixels, 0 to 10; 0: none. |
| `data` | string | yes | The picture file itself (PNG, JPEG or BMP), base64-encoded. |
| `file` | string | yes | The picture's file name. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The image's id, which its traced shapes name. |
| `invert` | boolean | yes | Carve the light parts instead of the dark ones. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The layer its traced shapes go on. |
| `min_area` | number | yes | Black or white specks smaller than this are dropped, mm², 0 to 100. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the picture's centre, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360. `x`, `y` and `width` are before the turn; the traced shapes are turned after the trace. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The picture's SHA-256. |
| `smoothing` | number | yes | How far a traced edge may be simplified away from the picture's edge, mm, 0.01 to 1. |
| `threshold` | [ImageThreshold](#imagethreshold) | yes | Grey values below this (0–255) are black: 1 to 254, or "auto" to pick it from the picture (Otsu's method). |
| `trace` | [ImageTrace](#imagetrace) | yes | What it is traced into: the black parts' outlines (for a V-carve) or their centre lines (for a follow path). |
| `width` | number | yes | The picture's width on the stock, mm; its height follows from the picture. |
| `x` | number | yes | X of the picture's lower-left corner on the stock, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Y of the picture's lower-left corner on the stock, mm. |

## ImageThreshold

Where grey turns black: "auto" or a grey value.

- [AutoThreshold](#autothreshold): Picked from the picture.

- integer: Grey values below this are black, 1 to 254.

## ImageTrace

What a picture is traced into.

- `"outline"`: Closed outlines round the black parts, black inside.

- `"centre_line"`: Open (or closed) paths along the black strokes' middles.

## InflateProfile

How an inflated shape rises from its edge.

- `"round"`: A quarter circle: steep at the edge, flat on top.

- `"straight"`: A straight rise: a ridge along narrow strokes.

## Instance

The part placed again (docs/specs/instances.md §2): mirrored, then turned, about the part's centre, then moved.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number | yes | Then turned about the part's centre, radians, counter-clockwise. |
| `at` | 2 × number | yes | Then moved, mm. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | False: kept, but not cut. |
| `id` | integer | yes | Its number in the part, from 2 (1 is the part as drawn). |
| `mirror` | [Mirror](#mirror) or null | no | Mirrored about the part's centre line first. Null: as drawn. |

## InstanceOrder

In which order a part and its instances are cut.

- `"by_operation"`: Each operation on every instance, then the next operation.

- `"by_instance"`: Every operation on one instance, then the next instance. Called `by_copy` before schema 38, and `by_part` before parts came (schema 22).

## IssueSeverity

One of: `"warning"`, `"error"`.

## Joint

The joint along a seam between two pieces (docs/specs/pieces.md §4).

- `"knobs"`: Round heads on narrower necks, alternating in and out, as on a jigsaw puzzle.

- `"fingers"`: Square teeth with rounded corners.

## Lead

Quarter-circle lead-in and lead-out.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | yes | Radius of the lead arcs, mm: more than 0, at most 10 tool diameters. Smaller where there's no room. |

## LineSegment

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | 2 × number | yes | End point, mm. |
| `start` | 2 × number | yes | Start point, mm. |

## Machine

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_post` | [CustomPost](#custompost) or null | no | Your own post-processor, copied into the project when chosen, so it gives the same G-code anywhere. Null: `post` is a built-in one. |
| `gcode_units` | [Units](#units) | yes | The units the G-code is written in: `mm` (G21) or `inch` (G20). Everything else in the project stays in mm. Since schema 28. |
| `library_uid` | string or null | no | The `uid` of the machine profile these values came from, for reference; nothing that cuts reads it. Null: not from a profile. |
| `max_feed` | number or null | no | The machine's fastest feed, mm/min: higher feeds are refused, and the cycle time uses it for rapids. Null: unknown. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The machine profile these values came from, for reference; nothing reads it. |
| `post` | string | yes | The post-processor: `grbl`, `linuxcnc`, `mach3`, or the name of your own. |
| `safe_z` | number | yes | The height for rapid moves sideways, mm above Z0. Above the stock top. |
| `spindle` | [Spindle](#spindle) | yes | The spindle's direction: `cw` (M3) or `ccw` (M4). |
| `tool_change` | [ToolChange](#toolchange) | yes | With several tools: `files` (one file per tool) or `program` (one file with tool changes). |
| `travel` | [Travel](#travel) or null | no | The machine's travel, mm. When set, a program that moves farther is refused. Null: not checked. |

## MaterialRef

A library material, as a project names it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `library_uid` | string | yes | The library material's uid. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name when chosen, shown when the library no longer has it. |

## Mirror

How a part is cut mirrored: about the vertical or the horizontal centre line of its box.

- `"left_right"`: About the vertical centre line: left and right change places, X is mirrored.

- `"top_bottom"`: About the horizontal centre line: top and bottom change places, Y is mirrored.

## Model

A 3D model (an STL file) carved as a relief from the top: the file itself, which way is up, and where it lies on the board. Its footprint outline is a `path` shape on its layer that names it in `model`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | string | yes | The STL file itself, base64-encoded. |
| `depth` | number | yes | How deep the relief goes, from the model's top to its lowest point, mm. |
| `file` | string | yes | The STL file's name. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The model's id, which its outline and reliefs name. |
| `keep` | number | no | The share of the turned model's height kept, from its top, more than 0 and at most 1: what lies below is cut away, its back (docs/specs/relief-wizard.md §5). Width, depth and the outline are the kept part's. 1 (the whole model) when missing. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The layer its footprint outline goes on. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name in the Browser and messages: the file's name without its extension at first. |
| `picture` | [PictureDepth](#picturedepth) or null | no | Missing: the model is an STL file. Present: `data` is a picture (PNG, JPEG or BMP) read as a depth map with these settings; `up` is `z` and `proportional` false. |
| `proportional` | boolean | yes | The depth follows the width, in the model's own proportion: made again whenever the model changes (decision 4). |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the footprint's centre, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The STL file's SHA-256. |
| `units` | [Units](#units) | yes | The unit the file was read in, for its size on import only: the model is placed by `width` (decision 2). |
| `up` | [ModelUp](#modelup) | yes | Which of the model's axes points up on the board. |
| `width` | number | yes | The footprint's width on the board, mm: it scales X and Y alike. |
| `x` | number | yes | X of the footprint's lower-left corner on the board, mm, before the turn. |
| `y` | number | yes | Y of the footprint's lower-left corner on the board, mm, before the turn. |

## ModelUp

Which of a model's axes points up on the board.

One of: `"z"`, `"y"`, `"x"`, `"-z"`, `"-y"`, `"-x"`.

## MouldEnds

How a moulding ends on an open path (docs/specs/moulding.md §4).

- object: The full profile right to the path's end.

- object: The profile turned a quarter round the path's end point.

- object: The section's depth fading to the surface over `length` mm at each end.

## MouldProfile

A moulding's cross-section (docs/specs/moulding.md §3): a built-in shape by its size, or a drawn open shape read as the section.

- object: A concave quarter circle: `radius` deep at the path, at the surface `radius` in.

- object: A convex quarter circle: the edge rounded, `radius` down at the path.

- object: An S, `width` wide and `depth` deep: a cove into a round-over, half the width each.

- object: A raised half round `2 × radius` wide, its top at the surface.

- object: A half-round groove `2 × radius` wide and `radius` deep.

- object: A drawn open shape, by id: across to the right, up the page; its leftmost point at the path, its highest point the surface.

## MouldSide

Which side of the path a moulding's profile lies on (docs/specs/moulding.md §4).

- `"left"`: Left of an open path as drawn.

- `"right"`: Right of an open path as drawn.

- `"inside"`: Inside a closed path.

- `"outside"`: Outside a closed path.

## Nest

A setup's nesting settings (docs/specs/nesting.md §10).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap` | number | yes | The least distance between what two instances cut, mm. |
| `margin` | number | yes | The least distance from what an instance cuts to the board's edge, mm. |

## Operation

### `"type": "profile"`

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clearance` | number | yes | How far the cut moves into the material that is kept, mm: positive removes more (a larger pocket, a smaller part), negative leaves material. Less than the tool radius. |
| `corner_choices` | list of [CornerChoice](#cornerchoice) | no | Corners with their own bone, whatever `corners` says. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `corners` | [Corners](#corners) or null | no | Dogbones or T-bones in the inside corners, so square parts fit. Null: the corners stay round. |
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional` milling. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut ends, mm down from the stock top. More than the start depth; below the stock bottom only within `stock.max_overcut`. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `finish` | [Finish](#finish) or null | no | A finishing pass: the roughing passes leave `stock` mm on the wall, and one last lap at full depth takes it off. Null: none. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the spiral ramp goes down along the contour, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). A profile always spirals down (docs/specs/profile-always-spiral.md). |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `side` | [Side](#side) | yes | Which side of the line the tool cuts: `outside` (cutting a part out), `inside` (a hole) or `on` the line. |
| `skin` | [Skin](#skin) or null | no | An onion skin: the passes stop `thickness` mm above the end depth, and one last lap cuts through it. Null: none. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |
| `starts` | list of 2 × number | no | Where the cut starts, as points in drawing coordinates (mm): each moves the start of the ring (contour) nearest to it. Empty: chosen by Chipload. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. The passes are equal, and the last one ends exactly at the end depth. |
| `tabs` | [Tabs](#tabs) or null | no | Holding tabs left at the bottom of the cut, so a part cut out doesn't come loose. Null: none. |
| `through` | number or null | no | Cut through the stock: how far below the stock bottom it ends, mm. The end depth is then the stock thickness plus this, and follows the thickness. Null: the end depth as set. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

### `"type": "pocket"`

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clearance` | number | yes | How far the cut moves into the material that is kept, mm: positive removes more (a larger pocket, a smaller part), negative leaves material. Less than the tool radius. |
| `corner_choices` | list of [CornerChoice](#cornerchoice) | no | Corners with their own bone, whatever `corners` says. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `corners` | [Corners](#corners) or null | no | Dogbones or T-bones in the inside corners, so square parts fit. Null: the corners stay round. |
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional` milling. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut ends, mm down from the stock top. More than the start depth; below the stock bottom only within `stock.max_overcut`. |
| `entry` | [Entry](#entry) | no | How the tool goes down at the start of each pass: `plunge` (straight down; needs a centre-cutting tool) or `ramp` along the path; pockets also `helix`. Missing: plunge. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `finish` | [PocketFinish](#pocketfinish) or null | no | A finishing pass: the roughing leaves `wall` mm on the walls and `floor` mm on the floor, then one level pass takes the floor and one lap each wall. Null: none. Left out when none. |
| `lead` | [Lead](#lead) or null | no | A quarter-circle lead-in and lead-out from the cleared side onto the wall. Null: none. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `rest` | [Rest](#rest) or null | no | Rest machining: clear only what a larger tool leaves in these shapes. Null: the whole pocket. |
| `rest_passes` | list of [ClearingPass](#clearingpass) | no | Rest passes: smaller endmills that clear what this pocket's tool (or the pass before) leaves, in its shapes and depths. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `slot_feed` | number or null | no | The feed of the rings that cut full width (those with no ring inside them), mm/min. Null: `feed`. |
| `slot_step_down` | number or null | no | The deepest each step of a full-width ring goes, mm: it goes down in such steps to each depth pass, before the other rings cut the pass at once. Null: `step_down`. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |
| `starts` | list of 2 × number | no | Where each wall ring starts, as points in drawing coordinates (mm): each moves the start of the wall ring nearest to it. Empty: chosen by Chipload. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. The passes are equal, and the last one ends exactly at the end depth. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between the clearing rings, as a fraction of the tool diameter: more than 0, at most 1. |
| `through` | number or null | no | Cut through the stock: how far below the stock bottom it ends, mm. The end depth is then the stock thickness plus this, and follows the thickness. Null: the end depth as set. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

### `"type": "vcarve"`

V-carve: a V-bit follows the centre line of closed shapes, as deep as makes the cut exactly as wide as the shape.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | The deepest the V-bit's tip may go, mm down from the stock top. Strokes that need more are carved to it, narrower than drawn, with a warning. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The feed, mm/min, for moves no steeper than 45°. |
| `floor` | [ClearingPass](#clearingpass) or null | no | A floor pass: an end mill that clears the floor between the walls of strokes too wide to carve from their centre line. Missing: none. Left out when missing. |
| `ignore_kinks_deg` | number | no | Corners where the outline turns by less than this, degrees (0 to 90), get no branch of the centre line: the bit doesn't rise into every kink. Missing: 0, every corner carved, as before the setting existed. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `passes` | integer | yes | How many depth passes, 1 to [`MAX_VCARVE_PASSES`]: each removes the same cross-section, the last at the end depth (docs/specs/v-carve.md decision 12). |
| `plug` | [Plug](#plug) or null | no | The plug of a V-carve inlay: the rest of the board is carved, its outline taken `plug.start_depth` below the surface, so the shapes stand as a tapered plug that fits the pocket a V-carve of the same shapes cuts. Missing: an ordinary V-carve. Left out when missing. |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed for moves steeper than 45°, mm/min. |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | The surface carved, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more to carve on a floor an earlier pocket cut. |
| `step_down` | number or null | no | An ordinary step down instead, mm: equal passes, none deeper than it, the last at the end depth, as in a pocket. Missing: passes of equal load (`passes`), which is kept meanwhile. Left out when missing. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

Chamfer: a V-bit's flank on the line of closed shapes, breaking their top edge.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |

## Part

A part: a named group of operations, cut together, with its own copies (docs/specs/parts.md §2). It owns no geometry: its operations select the shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number | yes | Instance 1, the part itself, turned about the part's centre, radians, counter-clockwise, as an instance is; 0: as drawn. Since schema 39. |
| `at` | 2 × number | yes | Instance 1 then moved, mm; (0, 0): where drawn. Since schema 39. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | False: the part and all its operations stay in the project but aren't cut. |
| `id` | integer | yes | Its number, unique in the project: what operations name it by. |
| `instances` | list of [Instance](#instance) | yes | The part placed again: each instance the same shapes and operations moved, turned and perhaps mirrored (instance 1 is the part itself, placed by `angle` and `at`, and isn't listed). Empty: cut once. Since schema 38, in place of a grid of copies. |
| `mirror` | [Mirror](#mirror) or null | no | Cut mirrored about the centre line of its box, the drawing as drawn. Missing: as drawn. Left out when missing. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name, unique in the project, shown in the Browser, the report and the sheet. |
| `order` | [InstanceOrder](#instanceorder) | yes | `by_operation`: each operation on every instance, then the next; `by_instance`: every operation on one instance, then the next instance. Since schema 38. |
| `setup` | integer | yes | The id of the setup it is cut in (`setups`). Since schema 34. |
| `turns` | [Turns](#turns) or null | no | How it may be turned when nested. Missing: a quarter turn at a time. Left out when missing. |

## PictureDepth

How a picture model's picture is read as heights (docs/specs/picture-relief.md §3).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | number | yes | Grey shares up to this, 0 to 0.95, are background, not the model; 0: none. |
| `gamma` | number | yes | The heights raised to this power, 0.2 to 5: above 1 flatter low ground and steeper tops. |
| `invert` | boolean | no | `inflate`: white is the shape; false: black is. |
| `mode` | [PictureMode](#picturemode) | no | How the picture becomes heights: a depth map, or its shapes inflated. Missing: a depth map. |
| `profile` | [InflateProfile](#inflateprofile) | no | `inflate`: how a shape rises from its edge. |
| `reach` | number or null | no | `inflate`: how far in from the edge the height grows, mm, more than 0; null: the widest shape's half-width. |
| `smoothing` | number | yes | A blur over the heights, its radius on the board, mm: 0 to 5. |
| `threshold` | integer or null | no | `inflate`: grey levels below this (1 to 254) are black; null: picked from the picture. |
| `white_high` | boolean | yes | White is the top, black the bottom; false: the other way round. |

## PictureMode

How a picture model's picture becomes heights (docs/specs/inflated-shapes.md §3).

- `"depth"`: Brightness as height.

- `"inflate"`: Its black-and-white shapes, each rising from its edge.

| `x` | number | yes |  |
| `y` | number | yes |  |

## Pieces

How a setup is cut in pieces (docs/specs/pieces.md §10).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `board` | [PieceBoard](#pieceboard) | yes | The boards the pieces are cut from: each piece, its joints and the setup's margin fit on one. |
| `clearance` | number | yes | The room between two pieces at a seam, mm, for glue: each side gives half. |
| `grid` | [PieceGrid](#piecegrid) or null | no | Columns and rows of pieces. Null: the fewest whose pieces fit the board. |
| `joint` | [Joint](#joint) | yes | The joints along the seams. |
| `shift_x` | list of number | no | Each inner seam between columns moved along X from its even position, mm, from the left. Missing ones: 0. |
| `shift_y` | list of number | no | Each inner seam between rows moved along Y from its even position, mm, from the bottom. Missing ones: 0. |
| `size` | number | yes | The joint's size, mm: a knob's head diameter, a finger's length. |
| `spacing` | number | yes | How far apart joints are along a seam, mm: knob to knob, or a finger and a gap. |

## Placement

Where the imported drawing is put: a DXF point p goes to scale · rotate(p) + (dx, dy), turned and scaled about the DXF's origin.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dx` | number | yes | Then moved along X, mm. |
| `dy` | number | yes | Then moved along Y, mm. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the DXF's origin, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360, after the scale. Multiples of 90 are exact. |
| `scale` | number | yes | Scaled about the DXF's origin by this factor, 0.001 to 1000; 1: as drawn. |

## Plug

A V-carve inlay's plug (docs/specs/vcarve-inlay.md §2.2).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the outline is taken, mm down from the stock top: more than the operation's start depth, less than its end depth. The end depth less this is the glue gap. |

## PocketFinish

A finishing pass on a pocket.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `floor` | number | yes | Left above the end depth by the roughing, mm: 0 or more, at most the step down, less than the cut; 0 on a pocket cut through. |
| `wall` | number | yes | Left on every wall by the roughing, mm: 0 or more, less than the tool radius. |

## RampShape

How a flute's ramp goes down from its end to the full depth.

- `"straight"`: Evenly: depth × u, u from 0 at the end to 1 at full depth.

- `"curved"`: Steepest at the surface, easing into the floor: depth × sin(π/2 × u).

## Register

How a turned board is located again.

- `"pins"`: Dowel pins through holes on the turn axis, drilled with the front.

- `"corner"`: Pushed into the same corner of a fence: the board's size must be exact.

## ReliefRim

A relief's rim (docs/specs/stl-relief.md §16): a flat at the floor round the area, then a ramp up to the stock top.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corner_radius` | number | no | `box` only: the radius of the flat's outer corners, mm, from 0 to the width. |
| `hull` | number | no | `outline` only: how far the outline is filled out towards its convex hull before the flat goes round it, 0 (as it is) to 1 (the hull). Missing: 0. |
| `ramp` | number | yes | The ramp's slope from the flat up to the stock top, radians from horizontal: from 10° to 90° (a straight wall). |
| `shape` | [RimShape](#rimshape) | yes | `outline`: the area's outer loops grown; `box`: the rectangle round them. |
| `width` | number | yes | The flat's width, mm from the outline or the rectangle: 0 or more. |

## ReliefRoughing

A relief's roughing pass (docs/specs/stl-relief.md §5): the material taken down in levels with the raster, an allowance left on the model for the finish.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowance` | number | yes | What is left on the model for the finish, mm, in every direction: 0 or more. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: kept, but not cut. Missing: true. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down to each stretch's first point, mm/min. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The distance between levels, mm. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between lines, as a fraction of the tool diameter: more than 0, at most 0.9. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`): an end mill or a plain ball nose. |

## ReliefSmoothing

A relief's smoothing pass (docs/specs/stl-relief.md §17): after the roughing, the surface followed once with the raster, an allowance left on the model for the finish.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowance` | number | yes | What is left on the model for the finish, mm, in every direction: 0 or more. |
| `angle` | number | yes | The lines' direction, radians counter-clockwise from X: across the roughing's by default. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: kept, but not cut. Missing: true. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down to each line's first point, mm/min. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between lines, as a fraction of the tool diameter: more than 0, at most 0.9. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`): an end mill or a plain ball nose. |

## Rest

Rest machining: the pocket clears only the material the larger tool `after_tool` can't reach in its shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after_tool` | integer | yes | The id of the larger project tool whose leftovers this pocket clears. |

## RimShape

What a relief's rim follows (docs/specs/stl-relief.md §16).

- `"outline"`: The area's outer loops, grown with round corners.

- `"box"`: The rectangle round the area's outer loops, grown, its corners rounded.

## Selector

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dxf` | integer or null | no | Only shapes from this DXF (an id in `drawing.dxfs`). |
| `exclude` | list of integer or null | no | Shapes of that DXF, image, text or group left out (ids); with `dxf`, `image`, `text` or `group` only. A contour with any of them isn't cut. A traced image's, or a text's, are found again when it is made again. |
| `group` | integer or null | no | The shapes and texts' letters of this group (an id in `drawing.groups`), as they are at each run. |
| `image` | integer or null | no | Only shapes traced from this image (an id in `drawing.images`). |
| `layer` | string or null | no | Every shape on this layer (upper or lower case don't matter). |
| `model` | integer or null | no | The footprint outline of this 3D model (an id in `drawing.models`). |
| `shapes` | list of integer or null | no | These shapes, by id. |
| `text` | integer or null | no | Only the letters of this text (an id in `drawing.texts`). |

## Setup

A setup: one board clamped once on the machine, with its stock and work zero, and the parts cut from it (docs/specs/setups.md §2).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `back_of` | [BackOf](#backof) or null | no | Set: this setup is the back of another, the same board turned over. Its stock and work zero then follow that setup's ([`Job::follow_fronts`]), and its cuts are mirrored about the board's centre line. Null: a board of its own. Since schema 36. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the setup and its parts stay in the project but aren't cut. |
| `id` | integer | yes | Its number, unique in the project: what parts name it by. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name, shown in the Browser, the report and the setup sheet. |
| `nest` | [Nest](#nest) or null | no | How the setup was last nested: its gap and margin, kept so *Nest again* needs no questions. Missing: never nested. Left out when missing. |
| `pieces` | [Pieces](#pieces) or null | no | Set: the setup is cut as a puzzle, in pieces that each fit a board, joined by seams with joints; each piece is a program of its own. Null: one board. Since schema 37. |
| `stock` | [Stock](#stock) | yes | The board. |
| `work_zero` | [WorkZero](#workzero) | no | The point of the drawing that becomes X0 Y0 in its G-code. Missing: the drawing's origin. |

## Shape

One shape of the drawing: imported from a DXF (`path`: lines and arcs, one shape per DXF entity), or drawn in Chipload (`circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`). One flat object: `id`, `layer`, `kind`, then the fields of that kind.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number or null | no | rectangle: its rotation about the centre; polygon: the angle of its first corner from +X; radians, counter-clockwise. |
| `bulges` | list of number or null | no | polyline: one per segment, as in DXF: tan(sweep / 4); 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise. |
| `center` | 2 × number or null | no | circle, rectangle, polygon: the centre, mm. |
| `closed` | boolean or null | no | path, polyline: whether it ends where it starts. |
| `construction` | boolean | no | circle, rectangle, polygon, polyline: construction geometry, shown and snapped to but never cut; left out when false. |
| `corner_radius` | number or null | no | rectangle: the radius of its corners, mm; 0 for sharp ones. |
| `dxf` | integer or null | no | path: the DXF it was imported from (its id in `drawing.dxfs`). |
| `dxf_handle` | string or null | no | path: the handle of the DXF entity it came from, which keeps its id when the DXF is updated. |
| `dxf_type` | string or null | no | path: the DXF entity's type, e.g. LWPOLYLINE. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The shape's id, which operations select it by. |
| `image` | integer or null | no | path: the image it was traced from; absent for shapes from a DXF. |
| `kind` | [ShapeKind](#shapekind) | yes | `path` (imported from a DXF), or a shape drawn in Chipload: `circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`. |
| `layer` | string | yes | Its layer. |
| `length` | number or null | no | rectangle: its size along its own X axis, mm. |
| `model` | integer or null | no | path: the 3D model it is the footprint outline of (its id in `drawing.models`). |
| `name` | string or null | no | circle, rectangle, polyline: its name in the Browser; left out when it has none. |
| `points` | list of 2 × number or null | no | polyline: its points, mm. |
| `radius` | number or null | no | circle: the radius, mm; polygon: the radius to its corners, mm. |
| `segments` | list of [PathSegment](#pathsegment) or null | no | path: its lines and arcs, mm. |
| `sides` | integer or null | no | polygon: how many sides (and corners) it has, 3 to 1000. |
| `text` | integer or null | no | path: the text it is a letter of (its id in `drawing.texts`). |
| `width` | number or null | no | rectangle: its size along its own Y axis, mm. |

## ShapeGroup

Drawn shapes and texts kept together: one click selects them all, and they move, turn, scale and are cut as one (docs/specs/shape-groups.md). A shape or text is in at most one group; groups don't hold groups.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes | The group's id, which operations' selectors name. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name in the Browser. |
| `rotation` | number | no | How far its box is turned, degrees counter-clockwise, in [0, 360): the turns it was given, so that its box turns with it (docs/specs/dxf-whole-on-canvas.md §6). 0 for a new group. |
| `shapes` | list of integer | no | Its drawn shapes, by id. |
| `texts` | list of integer | no | Its texts, by id, with their letters. |

## ShapeKind

One of: `"path"`, `"circle"`, `"rectangle"`, `"polyline"`, `"polygon"`.

## Side

One of: `"inside"`, `"outside"`, `"on"`.

## Skin

An onion skin on a profile.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thickness` | number | yes | Left above the end depth until the last lap, mm: more than 0, at most the step down. |

## SourceIssue

An import-time issue that can't be recomputed from the shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | What kind of issue, e.g. `duplicate` or `open_contour` (see the import page of the guide). |
| `message` | string | yes | What it is, in words. |
| `severity` | [IssueSeverity](#issueseverity) | yes | `warning` or `error`. |

## Spindle

- `"cw"`: M3

- `"ccw"`: M4

## Stock

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fit` | number or null | no | Centred on the drawing only: its size is the drawing's outline plus this margin each side, mm, following the drawing; `x` and `y` are then used only while the drawing is empty. Null: the size is `x` × `y`. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The project's material: new operations take it, with its values. Each operation names its own (`material` on the operation). Null: none. |
| `max_overcut` | number | yes | How far a cut may go below the stock bottom, into the spoilboard, mm. |
| `origin` | [StockOrigin](#stockorigin) | no | Where the stock lies: its `bottom_left` corner or its `center` at the drawing's origin, or centred on the drawing itself (`drawing`), following it. |
| `thickness` | number | yes | Thickness, mm. Depths count down from the top. |
| `x` | number | yes | Size along X, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Size along Y, mm. |
| `z_zero` | [ZZero](#zzero) | no | Where Z0 is: the stock `top` or `bottom`. |

## StockCorner

One of: `"center"`, `"bottom_left"`, `"bottom_right"`, `"top_left"`, `"top_right"`.

## StockOrigin

- `"bottom_left"`, `"center"`: 

- `"drawing"`: Centred on the drawing's outline, sticking out equally all round, and following the drawing when it moves or changes (the user, 2026-10-28). Construction geometry doesn't count; an empty drawing centres it on the origin.

## Tabs

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `along` | [Axis](#axis) or null | no | Where a ring without tabs placed by hand gets its `count` tabs: on its edges along `x` (bottom and top) or `y` (left and right), half on each. Left out: evenly round it. |
| `at` | list of 2 × number | no | Tab centres placed by hand, in drawing coordinates (mm): a contour with points gets exactly those tabs, one without gets `count`, evenly spaced. Left out when empty. |
| `count` | integer | yes | Tabs per contour, at least 1. |
| `flank_angle` | number | yes | The slope of the tab's sides, radians: π/2 (90°) straight, less for sloped tabs a ramped profile follows. |
| `height` | number | yes | The bridge's thickness, up from the bottom of the cut, mm. |
| `width` | number | yes | The bridge left on the part, along its edge, mm (the flat top of a sloped tab). |

## Text

A text written into shapes: what it says, its font and size, and where it goes. Its letters are `path` shapes on its layer that name it in `text`, made again when it changes; the font is needed only for that, not to cut them.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | [TextAlign](#textalign) | yes | How the lines line up against each other. |
| `anchor` | [TextAnchor](#textanchor) | no | What `x` and `y` are: the box's lower-left corner (before the turn), or its centre. A centred text stays centred there when its words, font or size change. Missing: the corner. |
| `font` | string | yes | The font: a built-in one (FreeSans, FreeSerif, …) or one on the computer, by its full name (`chipload text fonts`). Only its name is stored; its letters are the text's shapes, kept where the font isn't (docs/specs/system-fonts.md). |
| `height` | number | yes | The height of a capital letter, mm. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The text's id, which its letters name. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The layer its letters go on. |
| `line_spacing` | number | yes | From one line's base to the next, in capital heights. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the box's centre, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360. |
| `spacing` | number | yes | Extra space between letters, mm; 0: the font's own spacing, kerning included. |
| `text` | string | yes | What it says; a line break ("\n") starts a new line. |
| `x` | number | yes | X of the text's anchor on the stock, mm: the lower-left corner of its box (before the turn) or its centre. |
| `y` | number | yes | Y of the text's anchor on the stock, mm. |

## TextAlign

How a text's lines line up.

One of: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`.

## TextAnchor

What a text's position is (docs/specs/text.md §3).

- `"corner"`: The lower-left corner of the text's box, before the turn.

- `"center"`: The centre of the text's box (the turn keeps it in place).

## Tool

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number or null | no | V-bits: the included angle, radians. Null: unknown; a V-carve then refuses the tool. Ball noses: the taper's included angle; null: a plain ball nose. |
| `center_cutting` | boolean or null | no | Whether it can plunge straight down. False: profiles ramp in and pockets go down round a helix. Null: unknown. |
| `corner_radius` | number or null | no | End mills: the radius of its corners, mm, a bull nose (docs/specs/corner-radius.md §2). Missing: square corners. Left out of the file when missing, so a Chipload that doesn't know it refuses only a tool that has one. |
| `diameter` | number | yes | Diameter, mm. For a V-bit, its widest cutting diameter. |
| `flutes` | integer or null | no | Number of flutes, for the chip load. Null: unknown. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The tool's number: what operations name it by, and its T number in the G-code. |
| `library_uid` | string or null | no | The `uid` of the library tool it came from, for reference; nothing that cuts reads it. Null: not from the library. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The library tool it came from, for reference. |
| `rpm` | number or null | no | Spindle speed, rpm. Needed to generate. |
| `tip_diameter` | number or null | no | V-bits: the flat tip's diameter, mm. Null: pointed. Tapered ball noses: the ball's diameter at the tip. |
| `type` | [ToolType](#tooltype) | no | `endmill`, `drill`, `vbit` or `ballnose`. |

## ToolChange

How a job with several tools is written.

- `"files"`: One G-code file per tool group; the user changes the tool and sets Z zero between.

- `"program"`: One file with `T<n> M6` at each change, for a sender that handles it.

## ToolType

- `"endmill"`, `"drill"`, `"vbit"`: 

- `"ballnose"`: A ball nose, plain or tapered (docs/specs/stl-relief.md §8): for reliefs and follow paths only.

## Travel

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | yes | Travel along X, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Travel along Y, mm. |
| `z` | number | yes | Travel along Z, mm. |

## Turn

How a board is turned over: about its vertical or its horizontal centre line.

- `"left_right"`: About the vertical centre line: the left edge goes to the right, X is mirrored.

- `"top_bottom"`: About the horizontal centre line: the bottom edge goes to the top, Y is mirrored.

## Turns

How a part may be turned when it is nested (docs/specs/nesting.md §3): wood grain is the usual reason for none or half.

- `"none"`: As it lies.

- `"half"`: As it lies or turned 180°.

- `"quarter"`: A quarter turn at a time.

- `"every_15"`: 15° at a time.

## Units

One of: `"mm"`, `"inch"`.

## UnitsFrom

- `"dxf"`: Declared by the file: a DXF's $INSUNITS, an SVG's size in real units.

- `"user"`: The file declared none; the user chose (a DXF's units, an SVG's pixels per inch).

## Wall

One of a corner's two walls, by length.

One of: `"longer"`, `"shorter"`.

## WorkZero

Where the G-code's X0 Y0 is. The geometry never moves; only the output is translated.

- object: The drawing's own origin (the only choice before work_zero existed). An empty struct variant, not a unit one, so serde refuses stray fields here too.

- object: A corner or the centre of the stock, as placed by `stock.origin`.

- object: Any point, in drawing coordinates (mm).

## ZZero

One of: `"top"`, `"bottom"`.
